metadata.description: Monthly herd management calendar for Kenyan smallholder dairy farmers
metadata.target_animal: Friesian x Zebu crossbred (dominant smallholder type)
sources: Dairy Farmers Handbook, 9th ed. 2025, Farmers Helping Farmers/UPEI
Smallholder Dairy Farmer Training Manual, ILRI Manual 24, 2016

Dairy.description: Kenya smallholder dairy cow — predominantly Friesian x Zebu crossbred

housing_maintenance.action: Repair and clean housing during dry season — fix leaking roofs, broken drainage, and rotting floors before the long rains arrive. Ensure bedding is dry to prevent mastitis.

urgent.name: Housing maintenance — wet conditions increase urgency
urgent.risk: Wet, dirty housing is the main cause of mastitis and respiratory disease in dairy cattle
extra_actions: Fix drainage channels before rains continue — standing water must not pool in stalls
Add dry bedding (sawdust or dry grass) over wet floor
Check roof for leaks and repair immediately

routine.name: Housing maintenance — schedule now before rains
extra_actions: Check and clear all drainage channels
Inspect roof and repair before next rains
Top up bedding depth to 10–15 cm

vaccination.action: Administer FMD booster vaccination (first of two annual doses). Record animals vaccinated and due dates for the September dose.

suitable.name: Vaccination due — dry conditions, good to proceed
extra_actions: Record all animals vaccinated with date, batch number, and next due date

blocked.name: Vaccination due — wait for a dry day
blocked.risk: Wet conditions increase the risk of infection at the injection site
extra_actions: Wait for dry conditions before vaccinating
Record the postponement and reschedule within the same week

deworming.action: Strategic deworming at start of short dry season. Use broad-spectrum anthelmintic (e.g. albendazole or ivermectin). Rotate drug class annually to reduce resistance.

always.name: Strategic deworming due this month
always.risk: Internal parasites peak after rains — treat now before worm burden builds
extra_actions: Weigh animals first — dose by bodyweight, not estimate
Record product name, dose, and all animals treated

supplementary_feeding.action: Dry season forage quality and quantity declines sharply. Supplement with stored hay, silage, or concentrate to maintain body condition score (BCS) 3.0–3.5 ahead of calving.

acaricide_spraying.action: Fortnightly tick control programme during the dry season. Rotate acaricide class (e.g. amidine, synthetic pyrethroid) to manage resistance.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

body_condition_scoring.action: Score all cows in dry period. Target BCS 3.0–3.5 at calving. Adjust ration now — it is too late to correct condition score in the final 3 weeks before calving.

1.nutrition_notes: Forage quality lowest of the year. Provide hay or silage at minimum 3% of body weight (dry matter). Supplement with 1–2 kg/day dairy meal for cows approaching calving. Ensure continuous access to clean water (min 50 L/cow/day).

pre_calving_management.action: Implement 'steaming up' — increase concentrate to 2–3 kg/day in the 3 weeks before expected calving. Ensure cows calve at BCS 3.0–3.5. Separate cows due to calve within 1 week into a dedicated, clean, well-bedded calving pen.

housing_prep.action: Deep-clean and disinfect calving pens before the calving season. Lay fresh dry bedding (straw or wood shavings). Ensure calving area is sheltered from cold nights.

vaccination.action: Administer Blackquarter (BQ) and Haemorrhagic Septicaemia (HS) annual vaccination. Conduct brucellosis check/certification — important for milk safety and herd certification programmes.

suitable.name: Vaccination due — dry conditions, good to proceed
extra_actions: Record all animals vaccinated with date, batch number, and next due date

blocked.name: Vaccination due — wait for a dry day
blocked.risk: Wet conditions increase the risk of infection at the injection site
extra_actions: Wait for dry conditions before vaccinating
Record the postponement and reschedule within the same week

acaricide_spraying.action: Continue fortnightly tick control. Inspect udder and groin for tick burdens in pre-calving cows — high tick loads can cause stress during late pregnancy.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

water_access.action: Ensure all dry cows and heifers have clean water at all times. Dehydration in late pregnancy elevates retained placenta and calving difficulty risk.

2.nutrition_notes: Steaming-up period: increase energy-dense concentrate to 2–3 kg/day for 3 weeks pre-calving. Do NOT reduce roughage — fibre intake maintains rumen health and reduces milk fever risk. Avoid over-conditioning (BCS >3.5) which increases ketosis and calving problems.

calving_management.action: Attend all calvings. Feed newborn calf colostrum within 6 hours of birth (minimum 2 litres, ideally 3–4 litres). Record calving date, calf sex, and dam ID. Check for retained placenta (remove manually after 12 hours if not expelled). Monitor cows for milk fever and prolapse.

acaricide_spraying.action: Switch to weekly acaricide spraying as long rains begin — tick activity surges with rising humidity and vegetation. Pay special attention to calves, which have lower tick immunity.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

mastitis_monitoring.action: Conduct California Mastitis Test (CMT) on all freshly-calved cows within 1 week of calving. Observe foremilk before each milking for clots, watery milk, or blood. Treat clinical mastitis promptly with intramammary antibiotics.

calf_management.action: House calves separately from cows after colostrum feeding. Feed whole milk or milk replacer at 10% of body weight/day in two feeds. Offer calf starter concentrate and clean water from day 3.

pasture_management.action: Long rains signal rapid pasture regrowth. Avoid overgrazing — allow 21–28 days rest between grazings. Do not graze paddocks less than 15 cm tall to prevent soil poaching and re-infection with parasites.

3.nutrition_notes: Freshly-calved cows enter peak nutritional demand. Transition to full lactation ration: 2–3 kg dairy meal per 5 litres of milk produced above 5 litres maintenance. Rising pasture quality during long rains reduces supplement requirement — assess weekly.

acaricide_spraying.action: Maintain weekly acaricide programme. April is peak tick season — failure to spray increases East Coast Fever (ECF), Anaplasmosis, and Babesiosis risk dramatically. Check calves daily for tick burdens, especially around the ears and groin.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

mastitis_monitoring.action: Wet conditions and calving combine to create peak mastitis risk. Use CMT weekly on all lactating cows. Ensure post-milking teat dipping in iodine-glycerine solution (0.3–0.5% iodine). Keep bedding clean and dry — add fresh material daily in wet weather.

forage_management.action: Implement rotational grazing strictly to prevent overgrazing and pasture damage from wet-season poaching. Begin Napier grass and legume (e.g. Desmodium) planting in well-drained plots for dry season forage conservation.

calf_health.action: Wet, cold conditions increase calf scours (diarrhoea) and pneumonia risk. Ensure calf housing is draught-free, dry, and well-ventilated. Treat scours with oral rehydration salts — seek veterinary advice for bloody scours.

milking_hygiene.action: Wash udder with warm water and dry before milking. Use pre- and post-milking teat dip. Strip foremilk into a separate strip cup — do not contaminate the bulk milk with mastitic milk.

4.nutrition_notes: Peak lactation beginning for cows that calved in March. Maintain high-energy ration — under-nutrition now depresses milk yield for the entire lactation. Green pasture quality is high during long rains; balance with concentrate to avoid rumen acidosis from excess lush grass.

acaricide_spraying.action: Continue weekly acaricide spraying through end of long rains. As rains taper, tick populations peak before the dry-season decline — do not reduce frequency prematurely.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

deworming.action: Strategic post-long-rains deworming. Pasture larval burden peaks after wet season — treat all lactating cows, dry cows, and calves. Use anthelmintic class not used in January dose.

always.name: Strategic deworming due this month
always.risk: Internal parasites peak after rains — treat now before worm burden builds
extra_actions: Weigh animals first — dose by bodyweight, not estimate
Record product name, dose, and all animals treated

silage_making.action: OPTIMAL WINDOW for Napier grass silage — abundant, high-quality green material available. Harvest at 1–1.2 m height, chop to 2–3 cm, compact well in pits or bags, seal airtight. Target 4–6 tonnes DM per cow for dry season.

heat_stress_monitoring.action: As rains end, watch for rising temperatures combined with humidity. Signs of heat stress: increased respiration rate (>60 breaths/min), reduced feed intake, clustering near water. Ensure shade and fresh water access.

breeding_records.action: Record cows that calved in February–March and are now approaching optimal AI window (50–80 days post-calving). Observe for oestrus signs (restlessness, clear discharge, standing to be mounted).

5.nutrition_notes: Cows in peak lactation (2–3 months post-calving) have the highest energy demand of the productive cycle. Do not reduce concentrate below 1 kg per 3–4 litres of milk. Cut and carry fresh Napier grass to supplement declining pasture quality as dry season approaches.

breeding_ai.action: Priority AI breeding month for cows that calved in February–March and are now 50–80 days post-calving (optimal conception window). Detect oestrus twice daily (morning and evening). Call AI technician within 6–12 hours of confirmed standing oestrus. Target 365-day calving interval.

suitable.name: Artificial insemination (AI) window — conditions suitable
extra_actions: Check for standing heat 2–3 times daily (morning, midday, evening)
Call the AI technician 12–18 hours after standing heat is first observed

heat_warning.name: AI window — heat stress is reducing chances of pregnancy
heat_warning.risk: Extreme heat — chances of pregnancy drop 20–30% under severe heat stress
extra_actions: Schedule insemination for early morning when temperatures are lowest
Ensure shade and cool water before insemination to reduce cow stress

acaricide_spraying.action: Reduce to fortnightly as dry season reduces tick activity. Do not stop entirely — monitor tick burdens weekly and spray immediately if ticks found in numbers.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

forage_conservation.action: Harvest mature Napier grass and Rhodes grass for hay making. Dry hay in windrows for 3–5 days before baling or storing loose. Target minimum 200–300 kg hay per cow for dry season feeding.

water_management.action: Dry season water stress begins. Ensure water points are clean and cattle have access at least twice daily. Minimum 50 L/day for dry cows, 80–100 L/day for lactating cows.

milk_quality.action: Establish good milking records — record daily milk weight per cow. Identify cows declining faster than expected (possible subclinical mastitis or nutrition gap). Milk at consistent times — irregular milking intervals reduce yield.

6.nutrition_notes: Transition to dry season feeding. Green pasture declining rapidly. Supplement lactating cows with 2–3 kg/day dairy meal plus cut-and-carry Napier. Begin rationing stored silage/hay — calculate stock against expected dry season duration (June–September).

breeding_ai.action: Continue AI programme for cows not yet confirmed pregnant. For late calvers (March–April), this is the optimal AI window. Maintain accurate oestrus detection records. If cow fails to conceive after 3 AI attempts, arrange veterinary examination.

suitable.name: Artificial insemination (AI) window — conditions suitable
extra_actions: Check for standing heat 2–3 times daily (morning, midday, evening)
Call the AI technician 12–18 hours after standing heat is first observed

heat_warning.name: AI window — heat stress is reducing chances of pregnancy
heat_warning.risk: Extreme heat — chances of pregnancy drop 20–30% under severe heat stress
extra_actions: Schedule insemination for early morning when temperatures are lowest
Ensure shade and cool water before insemination to reduce cow stress

forage_conservation.action: Maximise hay and silage production while any green material remains. Prioritise Napier, fodder maize, and legume hays. Store in dry, raised, rodent-proof locations. Label date of storage — use oldest stock first.

water_management.action: July is peak dry season — water scarcity is most acute. Ensure water troughs are filled daily. Where boreholes or piped water are unavailable, arrange water trucking before crisis point. Dehydration reduces milk yield by 15–25% and conception rates by 10–20%.

heat_stress_management.action: Peak heat stress months (Jul–Aug). Provide shade trees or shade structures over resting areas. Graze in early morning and late afternoon; allow rest during peak heat (10 am–3 pm). Monitor respiration rates — above 80 breaths/min is severe stress.

acaricide_spraying.action: Fortnightly tick control. Tick pressure is medium during dry season but do not abandon the programme — disease-carrying ticks are present year-round.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

7.nutrition_notes: Dry season feeding at full effect. Ration stored forage carefully — do not feed more than needed. Supplement with 2 kg/day dairy meal per lactating cow. Urea-treated straw (3% urea solution, 7-day fermentation) can extend low-quality roughage value. Monitor BCS monthly.

pregnancy_confirmation.action: Pregnancy diagnose cows bred in June–July (60–90 days post-AI is optimal for rectal palpation or ultrasound by vet/AI technician). Cows confirmed in calf: plan dry-off date (lactation days 275–285). Cows not in calf: arrange repeat AI or consider culling decision.

forage_planting_prep.action: Prepare land for forage planting in anticipation of short rains (October). Apply manure and phosphate fertiliser to plots. Plan Napier splits, Sudan grass, and fodder legume seed stocks.

water_management.action: Continue rigorous water provision. August is the second peak dry month. Check water source levels — rainwater harvesting tanks should be monitored. Prioritise lactating cows and late-pregnant animals for water access.

heat_stress_management.action: Continued heat stress peak. Avoid heavy physical work (herding, loading) during midday heat. If night temperatures stay above 20°C, supplement energy in the ration as cattle cannot eat during peak heat.

acaricide_spraying.action: Maintain fortnightly tick spraying programme. As short rains approach in October, tick populations will surge again — a robust programme now prevents re-infestation.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

8.nutrition_notes: Monitor BCS — cows should not drop below BCS 2.5 at this stage. If BCS is declining rapidly, increase concentrate or urea-treated straw. Cows in late lactation (month 8–10) have lower milk yield and can tolerate slightly reduced concentrate, but forage should remain ad libitum.

forage_planting.action: Plant fast-establishing fodder crops ahead of short rains — Boma Rhodes grass, Brachiaria (Mulato II), Sudan grass, and fodder cowpea. Sow in prepared seedbeds. Napier splits can be planted now for establishment before rains.

suitable.name: Forage planting window — rain providing good conditions
extra_actions: Plant Napier grass cuttings or seed Boma Rhodes/Brachiaria while soil is moist
Apply basal fertiliser (DSP) at planting into moist soil

blocked.name: Forage planting window — prepare land now, plant on first rain
blocked.risk: Planting into dry soil causes poor germination and establishment failure
extra_actions: Prepare land and source planting material now
Plant within 3 days of first significant rain (above 5 mm)

vaccination.action: Annual FMD vaccination — second dose of the year. Record all animals vaccinated. Timing before the short rains (October) is strategic as animal movement increases disease spread risk.

suitable.name: Vaccination due — dry conditions, good to proceed
extra_actions: Record all animals vaccinated with date, batch number, and next due date

blocked.name: Vaccination due — wait for a dry day
blocked.risk: Wet conditions increase the risk of infection at the injection site
extra_actions: Wait for dry conditions before vaccinating
Record the postponement and reschedule within the same week

housing_maintenance.action: Pre-rains housing inspection and maintenance. Repair all roof leaks, drainage channels, and floor drainage before October rains arrive. Replace bedding material — accumulated dry-season bedding must be composted.

urgent.name: Housing maintenance — wet conditions increase urgency
urgent.risk: Wet, dirty housing is the main cause of mastitis and respiratory disease in dairy cattle
extra_actions: Fix drainage channels before rains continue — standing water must not pool in stalls
Add dry bedding (sawdust or dry grass) over wet floor
Check roof for leaks and repair immediately

routine.name: Housing maintenance — schedule now before rains
extra_actions: Check and clear all drainage channels
Inspect roof and repair before next rains
Top up bedding depth to 10–15 cm

acaricide_spraying.action: Fortnightly acaricide application continues. September is the last month of lower tick pressure — prepare stocks of acaricide for the weekly programme starting in October.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

dry_off_planning.action: Identify cows due for drying off in October (10 months post-calving or as planned). Begin reducing milkings from 2x/day to 1x/day in the final 2 weeks before dry-off. Do not abruptly stop milking high-yielding cows.

9.nutrition_notes: Late lactation cows naturally reduce milk yield. This is an opportunity to improve body condition before dry-off. Target BCS 3.0–3.5 at drying off. Supplement with 1–2 kg/day dairy meal if BCS is below target. Stored forage supplies should last to October rains.

drying_off.action: Implement dry-off for cows completing 305-day lactation. At final milking, infuse ALL four quarters with Dry Cow Therapy (DCT) antibiotic tubes (e.g. cloxacillin or amoxicillin long-acting). Apply teat sealant after DCT infusion. Move dried-off cows to separate, clean dry-cow group.

always.name: Dry-off period — cows due for drying off this month
always.risk: An inadequate dry period reduces next lactation yield and raises mastitis risk
extra_actions: Infuse dry cow therapy (DCT) antibiotic tubes into all four quarters at dry-off
Check udder daily for the first 2 weeks after dry-off for swelling or heat
Reduce feed to a low-energy ration to help milk production stop gradually

acaricide_spraying.action: Switch back to weekly acaricide spraying as short rains begin — tick populations surge. October–November is second peak tick season. Ensure all animals are sprayed, including recently dried-off cows and young stock.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

forage_planting.action: SHORT RAINS PLANTING WINDOW — plant Napier grass splits, Brachiaria, fodder legumes (Desmodium, Leucaena), and fodder maize for silage. Establish now to have forage ready for the next dry season.

suitable.name: Forage planting window — rain providing good conditions
extra_actions: Plant Napier grass cuttings or seed Boma Rhodes/Brachiaria while soil is moist
Apply basal fertiliser (DSP) at planting into moist soil

blocked.name: Forage planting window — prepare land now, plant on first rain
blocked.risk: Planting into dry soil causes poor germination and establishment failure
extra_actions: Prepare land and source planting material now
Plant within 3 days of first significant rain (above 5 mm)

mastitis_surveillance.action: Inspect dry cows for swollen, painful quarters in first 2 weeks after dry-off — indicates DCT failure or new infection. Monitor closely as wet season begins. Maintain post-milking teat dip on lactating cows.

calf_health.action: Calves born in June–August are now 2–4 months old. Check growth rates and health status. Begin weaning calves from milk at 3–4 months by gradual reduction. Offer good quality starter concentrate and pasture.

10.nutrition_notes: Dried-off cows require only maintenance ration — 2–3 kg/day supplementary feed on top of available pasture and roughage. Avoid overfeeding dry cows — over-conditioned cows (BCS >4) have higher calving difficulty and metabolic disease risk. Lactating cows benefit from recovering pasture quality.

dry_cow_management.action: Monitor all dry cows daily for signs of mastitis, vaginal discharge, or poor body condition. Check that teat canal seal (from DCT/teat sealant) is intact — quarantine any cow showing udder swelling for veterinary treatment. Provide adequate nutrition for BCS gain if needed.

acaricide_spraying.action: Maintain weekly acaricide spraying through peak short-rains tick season. Monitor for acaricide resistance — if ticks survive 48 hours post-spray, switch to a different chemical class. East Coast Fever is the most economically damaging tick-borne disease in Kenya.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

deworming.action: Post-short-rains strategic deworming (third annual dose). Treat all categories: lactating cows, dry cows, and calves. High pasture larval burden after October–November rains. Use a third anthelmintic class if possible.

always.name: Strategic deworming due this month
always.risk: Internal parasites peak after rains — treat now before worm burden builds
extra_actions: Weigh animals first — dose by bodyweight, not estimate
Record product name, dose, and all animals treated

forage_assessment.action: Assess forage planted in October — Napier splits establishing, fodder legumes germinating. Topdress with CAN (50 kg/acre) to accelerate growth. Plan first harvest of new Napier at 4 cuts/year cycle.

pre_calving_prep.action: Cows dried off in October are now 4–5 weeks into dry period. Confirm calving dates for December–January calvers. Clean and prepare calving pens. Ensure colostrum plan is in place (bank colostrum from high producers if needed).

11.nutrition_notes: Short rains improve pasture quality and quantity — this is an opportunity to rebuild body condition in dry cows. Supplement dry cows at 2–3 kg/day concentrate in last 3 weeks before calving (steaming up). Lactating cows should benefit from improved pasture — adjust concentrate accordingly to avoid over-supplementation.

housing_maintenance.action: End-of-year housing inspection and deep clean. Compost manure heaps. Fix all drainage and floor issues identified during the wet season. Prepare the farm record system — review production records, breeding records, and health treatments for the year.

urgent.name: Housing maintenance — wet conditions increase urgency
urgent.risk: Wet, dirty housing is the main cause of mastitis and respiratory disease in dairy cattle
extra_actions: Fix drainage channels before rains continue — standing water must not pool in stalls
Add dry bedding (sawdust or dry grass) over wet floor
Check roof for leaks and repair immediately

routine.name: Housing maintenance — schedule now before rains
extra_actions: Check and clear all drainage channels
Inspect roof and repair before next rains
Top up bedding depth to 10–15 cm

vaccination.action: Annual vaccination review — confirm all animals received FMD (twice), BQ/HS (once), and any leptospirosis or lumpy skin disease vaccines recommended locally. Plan vaccination calendar for the coming year.

suitable.name: Vaccination due — dry conditions, good to proceed
extra_actions: Record all animals vaccinated with date, batch number, and next due date

blocked.name: Vaccination due — wait for a dry day
blocked.risk: Wet conditions increase the risk of infection at the injection site
extra_actions: Wait for dry conditions before vaccinating
Record the postponement and reschedule within the same week

body_condition_scoring.action: Score all cows — dry cows should be BCS 3.0–3.5 heading into January calving season. Cows below BCS 2.5 need intensive supplementation immediately. Cows above BCS 3.5 should be restricted to avoid metabolic problems at calving.

acaricide_spraying.action: Short rains tapering in December. Weekly spraying continues while vegetation remains lush. Switch to fortnightly in late December as conditions dry. Stock adequate acaricide for the January–February programme.

suitable.name: Acaricide treatment due — good conditions to spray today
extra_actions: Ensure full body coverage — ears, tail base, udder, and groin
Rotate acaricide type every 3 months to prevent tick resistance

blocked.name: Acaricide treatment due — wait for dry, calm conditions
blocked.risk: Rain washes acaricide off before it works; wind causes drift and missed coverage
extra_actions: Wait for a dry morning with low wind before spraying
Hand-remove any engorged ticks from sensitive areas (teats, ears) as a temporary measure

herd_records.action: Complete annual herd records. Calculate: calving rate, conception rate, milk yield per cow per year, calf mortality, disease incidence. Use data to identify underperforming animals and plan culling and replacement decisions.

12.nutrition_notes: December is transition from short rains to short dry season. Pasture quality declining. Ensure hay and silage stocks are adequate for January–February. Dry cows approaching calving in January need steaming-up concentrate (2–3 kg/day) in final 3 weeks. Ensure mineral supplementation (calcium, phosphorus, magnesium) for pre-calving cows to reduce milk fever.

herd_lifecycle_reference.dry_cow_therapy: Infuse DCT antibiotic tubes at dry-off in all quarters
